fields.description: What this society calls this piece of work: Flood Response, Blood Drive Support, Branch First Aid Duty. Display only; nothing in this app reads it to decide anything, and no deployment name appears in any source file.
fields.label: Title of Mission

fields.description: The stable business key, and the docname. A deployment and a deployment request point at these terms by this key, so relabelling the terms next year never rewrites what happened this year. This follows core's rule that configuration vocabularies are keyed by their stable business key while records about people and places get opaque IDs.
fields.label: Key

fields.description: The programme of work these terms are written under. Optional, because a society that runs standing duties rather than programmes has terms belonging to no project, and the terms written before this field existed belong to none either. Where it is set, the project is printed at the head of the terms of reference and its own closure stops new terms being written under it. A deployment reaches its project through its terms and never stores a second copy of the answer.
fields.label: Project

fields.description: Whether these terms are still offered for new work. Distinct from the submit state, and deliberately so: submitting freezes the wording, because accepting a deployment under these terms is accepting exactly this document. Retiring is the ordinary end of a piece of work and must leave every deployment already run under it intact, which cancelling a submitted document would not. So a terms of reference is submitted once and un-ticked here when the society stops using it.
fields.label: Is Active

fields.description: When the mission is expected to begin. Optional and never a rule: it is offered as the default when a deployment is set up under these terms, and the deployment's own start date is what governs from then on. Terms written for standing work — a branch first aid rota, a year-round blood drive — have no mission window at all, and leaving this empty says so.
fields.label: Expected Start Date

fields.description: When the mission is expected to end. Refused if it falls before the expected start date. Like the start date, a planning figure that a deployment may override.
fields.label: Expected End Date

fields.description: How many days a deployment under these terms usually runs for. A default offered when a request is raised, never a rule: the deployment's own start and end dates are what govern. Zero means the society has no usual length for this work.
fields.label: Usual Duration (Days)

fields.description: The part of the organisational tree these terms may be used in: that node and everything beneath it. A deployment or a request anchored outside it is refused. Left empty, the terms apply anywhere, which is what a society that has not narrowed them means. Containment is decided by core's geo adapter, so no depth and no level name is assumed.
fields.label: Geo Scope

fields.description: What a deployment under these terms is for, in the society's own words. One or two sentences: this is the line that appears wherever the terms are named in a list. Read by whoever raises a request and by whoever approves it; never read by code.
fields.label: Purpose

fields.description: The situation this mission answers to, at whatever length it takes: what happened, what is needed, what has already been done. Rich text because this is the part a society lifts from a situation report or takes to a donor, and stripping its formatting would make it worse paperwork rather than better data. Printed at the head of the terms of reference and offered as the deployment's opening note. Never read by code.
fields.label: Mission Background

fields.description: Who this mission has to deal with, and how to reach them. Printed on the terms of reference so a deployed volunteer carries the contacts on the paper they were given, rather than having to ask for them once they have arrived.
fields.label: Stakeholders

fields.description: What this mission sets out to achieve, one objective per row. Numbered on the printed document in the order they appear here.
fields.label: Objectives

fields.description: What the mission will leave behind: a register updated, a community trained, a report filed. Kept apart from the objectives because a society reporting on a deployment afterwards reports against these.
fields.label: Expected Outputs

fields.description: How the work will be done, chosen from the society's own VMMS TOR Methodology register with a note on what each method means for this mission. A Link rather than free text so a society can eventually report across missions on how it works.
fields.label: Approach Methodology

fields.description: The plan by day: what happens, when, and who leads it. Every dated row must fall inside the mission's own expected period where one is set, which is checked on save — an itinerary that runs past the end of the mission is a mistake worth catching on the form rather than in the field.
fields.label: Itinerary

fields.description: What the mission needs and what it is expected to cost. Each row's total is computed from its quantity and unit cost on save. Nothing in this app totals these across a project or reconciles them against actual spend: money paid to volunteers flows through VMMS Stipend Payment Form, which is anchored to a geography and a period rather than to a mission, and bridging the two is a decision nobody has taken yet.
fields.label: Resources

fields.description: The certifications a volunteer needs to be a candidate for this work. Each row is either mandatory (a hard filter) or desirable (a preference that ranks). Matching computes whether a held certification has lapsed at the moment of asking, so a volunteer whose training expired yesterday drops out of the candidate list today without anything having been written down.
fields.label: Required Certifications

fields.description: What a volunteer deployed under these terms is expected to do, in the society's own words. This is the substance of a terms of reference for the person reading it, and it is deliberately free text: a structured task vocabulary would be a second list to reconcile with every society's own paperwork.
fields.label: Responsibilities

fields.description: Whether a request to deploy under these terms needs somebody to authorise it. direct: there is no approver, and the request is fulfilled by whoever raises it. routed: the VMMS approval engine routes it to a resolved person, who approves or rejects it, and the request cannot become a deployment until they do. This is the same shape a membership type's approval_mode has, and it is read the same way: deployment/services/approval.py dispatches through two tables keyed by this value, and no source file compares it to a Terms of Reference name or to a stage label. Choosing routed requires a VMMS Approval Workflow governing VMMS Deployment Request; without one the request is refused, loudly, rather than quietly deploying unapproved.
fields.label: Approval Mode

fields.description: Anything about these terms that is not a field.
fields.label: Notes

fields.description: Set by Frappe when a submitted terms of reference is amended. The amendment is a new document with its own key, and the deployments already run under the original keep pointing at the original — which is the whole reason these are submittable. Somebody who accepted a mission accepted the wording that was in front of them, and an amendment must not reach back and change it.
fields.label: Amended From
